if you're not just a complete lemming they don't want you on a jury.

This is somewhat true, but there are limits in place for how many people each side can remove. Obviously each side wants as many jurors who side with their case as possible. How it normally works is an attorney for each side gets to ask questions to the jury pool. Once the questions are all done, jurors can be struck for cause, which means they have some inherent reason for not being able to function on a jury. For example, if english isn't their first language or they have a religious belief that prohibits them from casting judgment on others. Then each side gets to strike a certain number of jurors, but it is limited. Whatever is left is the jury. This is why your jury pool of 20 people seems like a lie. A normal jury pool will have 36 or 42 people for a 12 person jury. Say 5 get struck for cause. Each side then gets to strike the 6 jurors that will hurt their case the most. Then the first 12 jurors still left will be put on the jury with the next two kept as alternates.
